basic_identification.full_title: Composite Bottom for Stainless Steel Cooking Utensils — Specification (सम्मिश्र तलें के स्टेनलेस स्टील के पकाने के बर्तन — विशिष्टि)
basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering / Utensils, Cutlery and Domestic Hardware (approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Utensils, Cutlery and Domestic Hardware Sectional Committee, MED 33, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Utensils, Cutlery and Domestic Hardware Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements for materials, design, manufacture, dimensional limits, and physical-thermal testing of composite bottoms (sandwich, clad, or encapsulated designs) of stainless steel cooking utensils to ensure high thermal conductivity, rapid heat distribution, and durable joint adhesion.

version_status_and_amendments.supersedes: IS 4536 (Parts 1 to 3) (which historically covered copper electro-deposited, 3-ply construction, and copper-clad bottoms of stainless steel utensils)

allied_standards.title: Stainless Steel Utensils — Specification (First Revision)
allied_standards.relevance: The master standard for domestic stainless steel utensils, which designates that any sandwich-bottom, clad-bottom, or induction-bottom cookware must have its thermal-adhesion core designed and tested under IS 15960.

allied_standards.title: Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)
allied_standards.relevance: Regulates high-integrity domestic pressure cookers, requiring that their induction-compatible or composite bottoms successfully pass the physical adhesion and dry-heat quench tests of IS 15960.

allied_standards.title: Tri-Ply Clad Materials for Cookware — Specification
allied_standards.relevance: Regulates multi-layered clad raw sheets (stainless steel–aluminium–stainless steel), sharing parallel high-temperature thermal cycling and peel-adhesion requirements with IS 15960.

allied_standards.title: Handles for non-powered material handling/domestic utensils — Specification
allied_standards.relevance: Regulates the structural, load-bearing, and thermal insulation properties of handles secured to cooking utensils.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice on Occupational Safety and Health Audit
allied_standards.relevance: Directs safety audits in industrial manufacturing plants where sheet drawing, high-pressure brazing, and metal annealing represent severe mechanical and thermal safety hazards.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice for General Steel Construction
allied_standards.relevance: The master structural steel code in India, regulating support steelwork, structural frames, and overhead cranes used to carry heavy coiled steel coils in metal press shops.

allied_chemical_specifications.title: Dissolved Iron Testing — Spectrophotometric Method
allied_chemical_specifications.relevance: Provides high-precision chemical limits to evaluate dissolved trace iron leaching during boiling chemical staining tests on stainless steel cookware.

allied_chemical_specifications.title: Volumetric and Spectrophotometric Estimation of Iron
allied_chemical_specifications.relevance: Specifies volumetric estimation of iron using potassium permanganate and potassium bichromate to calibrate raw steel alloy compositions.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Mechanical Engineering Department / Utensils and Hardware)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Certification. However, under the Cookware and Utensils (Quality Control) Order 2024 issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, many categories of cookware are under mandatory BIS certification (effective 1 September 2024). This requires all composite-bottom stainless steel cookware manufactured or imported into India to carry the prestigious physical ISI 'Standard Mark' stamped on the steel body, certifying strict compliance with IS 15960.

requirements.detail: Under the active Amendment No. 1 (June 2024), the stainless steel sheet used to manufacture the utensil body must conform to designations X07Cr18Ni9 or X04Cr19Ni9 of IS 5522 or IS 6911, or to grades N1, N2, or N3 of IS 15997.
requirements.clause_reference: Clause 3.1 as amended by Amendment No. 1

requirements.detail: Requires bonding high-purity, wrought aluminium (conforming to IS 21) or pure copper to the bottom of the stainless steel vessel. This utilizes the thermal conductivity of the inner core to eliminate localized 'hot spots' that cause food burning, while maintaining a hygienic steel cooking surface.

Bond strength is evaluated using a specialized drop-impact rig. A steel ball weighing exactly half a kilogram (500 g) is dropped from a vertical height of 500 mm (0.5 m) directly onto the center of the composite bottom.
Following repeated impact cycles of the 500g steel ball, the composite bottom must show zero cracking, peeling, joint separation, or visual delamination.

To simulate real-world dry-boiling, the utensil is dry-heated to a temperature of 250°C to 260°C and immediately quenched in cold water at ambient temperature, repeating this cycle for 25 consecutive times.
Following the 25 thermal shock dry-heat quench cycles, the composite base must show zero blisters, separations, peeling, or joint failures under physical inspection.
The finished utensil is degreased in acetone and submerged for 16 hours in boiling chemical solutions of 99% Glacial Acetic Acid and Sodium Chloride maintained at 60°C ± 2°C.
The stainless steel cooking surface must show zero signs of pitting, discoloration, rust staining, or localized corrosion following the 16-hour chemical exposure.

All observed or calculated test and analytical values (such as sheet thickness, impact heights, and temperatures) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15960 : 2013 (Amended 2024) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing requirements for composite bottoms (sandwich, clad, or encapsulated bases) on stainless steel cooking utensils. Developed under the Utensils, Cutlery and Domestic Hardware Sectional Committee (MED 33) and amended in June 2024, the standard unifies materials, dimensions, and performance testing for cookware in India. It regulates the chemical designations of stainless steel sheets used for vessel bodies, specifies high-conductivity heat-spreader cores (aluminium or copper), and mandates strict physical-thermal tests—including a 500g steel ball impact drop test, multiple dry-heat water quench thermal cycling tests, and boiling acid staining exposures—to ensure that the heat-conducting bottom does not peel off, blister, or delaminate under high thermal stresses in residential and commercial kitchens.
